title: Bittensor Daily News: November 22, 2026

updates.headline: SN24 ms.computer opens website entries with a December 6 deadline
updates.summary:
SN24 ms.computer opened its website-building competition on November 21, following the planned event covered yesterday. The team offers 2,424 SN24 alpha from owner emissions: 1,024 for first place, 800 for second and 600 for third.

Anyone can enter up to three websites. Participants build and host their sites on ms.computer, then submit the live URLs in the official entries channel. Entries close December 6 at noon Central time, with winners scheduled for December 7.

The new information is the actual opening, entry limits and deadline. Free hosting itself is not a new launch. Database support, custom domains and payment functionality mentioned alongside the announcement remain future plans rather than features verified as available today.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars under the competition cap: a live entry window, prize breakdown and deadline are useful participant news. Two would understate those concrete terms; four would overrate a routine competition.

updates.headline: SN62 Ridges details Ridgeline pricing and locked-alpha credits
updates.summary:
Following the November 19 Ridgeline launch covered in our November 20 edition, SN62 Ridges' documentation now provides concrete access terms. The listed subscription is $9.99 a month for 10 credits. One credit runs one GitHub issue through the pull-request workflow; a pull-request review costs 0.1 credit.

The staking-credit route requires locked SN62 alpha, not simply holding the token. The guide lists one credit per 1,000 locked alpha every three days, with credits expiring after two weeks and synchronization potentially taking several hours.

Review requests require a linked Ridgeline account and repository write access. They use the requesting user's credits rather than automatically charging another repository member. Reviews can provide line-level findings, but producing a proposed fix still costs one credit. These are documented service terms reviewed November 22, not independently measured bug-fix quality or a second launch announcement.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: concrete pricing and eligibility affect prospective users beyond minor housekeeping. Four would overstate a terms follow-up to an already covered launch.

updates.headline: SN111 Claims opens its revised testnet round; submission cutoff has passed
updates.summary:
SN111 Claims opened its schema v1.1 testnet round on November 21 at 21:18 UTC, according to the team and published participation guide. The revised submission cutoff was November 22 at 11:00 UTC, which had already passed by this report's morning review. This updates yesterday's planned opening rather than announcing an entry window that is still open.

The round uses testnet subnet 530 and a flat set of 10 papers, starting from the reference baseline without the prescreen and screen stages. Its limits include $0.10 per paper, a two-million-token ceiling, 32,768 output tokens per call and 4 GiB of RAM. The guide allows 30 minutes for execution plus 10 minutes for installation.

Evaluation follows the cutoff and package checks. Results and the separately planned mainnet opening have not been verified. Participants should follow the official channel for the next round rather than assume the earlier mainnet timetable has been executed.

ecosystem.headline: TaoStats explains the MEV ordering route addressed in runtime 492
ecosystem.summary:
TaoStats published a technical investigation on November 21 explaining how a Bittensor trading bot used a later transaction to steer an earlier EVM contract call. Its researchers say they reported the mechanism privately to the OpenTensor Foundation before publication.

The signal was encoded in the tip on a failing set_heap_pages transaction. Its Operational classification gave it priority, allowing the contract to read the resulting balance change as trading instructions. The merged fix limits the payment wrapper's special Operational priority to calls signed by the sudo account, preventing ordinary wallets from using that particular shortcut.

TaoStats reports that runtime 492 activated the fix at block 9,542,321 on November 19. The merged implementation is verified here; the activation block is attributed to the researchers. Their report says the known bots stopped trading before activation and moved stake to root. It does not establish aggregate losses, and closing this ordering route does not mean all MEV has been eliminated.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: a documented protocol-level trading mitigation and its mechanism have consequences beyond routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established by a bounded route without demonstrated network-wide loss or disruption.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a documented protocol-level trading mitigation and its mechanism have consequences beyond routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established by a bounded route without demonstrated network-wide loss or disruption.
ratingAssessment.evidence: TaoStats investigation, November 21; Merged Operational-priority fix
ratingAssessment.scope: Published technical investigation and merged priority restriction.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Activation and bot behavior are attributed to TaoStats; no independent loss total or universal MEV protection established.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 494 candidate adds paid commitments and mechanism-specific delegation
ecosystem.summary:
The runtime 494 pull request was merged on November 20. Its official upgrade guide still describes a release candidate, so this report does not present the changes as activated on Finney.

The candidate adds optional burn-for-commit channels: when configured, a coldkey pays a TAO burn to publish a commitment to a particular mechanism and channel. This is disabled unless configured, ordinary transaction fees still apply, and legacy commitments remain separate. Validators can also authorize a delegate for one mechanism without transferring stake, ownership or validator status.

The default interval for owner emission-vector updates changes from 50,400 to 360 blocks. That concerns owner eTAO allocation updates, not the frequency of miner weight updates. Basket-trading controls become configurable, but the documented defaults retain the 2% slippage band and existing price-reference and refill behavior. A proposed 5% setting is a separate governance action, not an automatic default in this candidate. Integrators need the new runtime metadata.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: new protocol interfaces and owner/validator controls exceed routine three-star maintenance. Five is not established by a candidate whose activation and practical impact remain unverified.
